raw.rationale: The presence of recurrent, intermittent, painless hematuria with 70% dysmorphic red cells on phase-contrast microscopy is highly suggestive of a glomerular origin of bleeding, which is consistent with IgA nephropathy.

rejected.label: Thin basement membrane nephropathy
rejected.why: Typically presents with isolated hematuria, but the presence of dysmorphic red cells and the clinical context do not strongly support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Nephrolithiasis
rejected.why: The presence of small stones in the left kidney could contribute to hematuria, but the clinical presentation and laboratory findings suggest a glomerular cause

rejected.label: Alport syndrome
rejected.why: Typically presents with a family history of kidney disease, hearing loss, and eye abnormalities, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Medullary sponge kidney
rejected.why: Characterized by the presence of ectatic and cystic changes in the collecting ducts, which are not described in the abdominal ultrasonogram
